codeReview.summary: The implementation covers most lifecycle startup behaviors (ordering, dry-run, lockfile, health checks, partial failures, localhost binding, and API-key env propagation), but two blocking gaps remain versus the feature contract.

issues.description: Missing-model handling is not implemented. The startup loop goes straight from port checks to process launch/health polling, but there is no preflight check that the referenced tier model/source is actually present locally (or a targeted missing-model error path). This does not satisfy the feature requirement to handle missing models explicitly and can degrade into generic startup timeout/failure behavior instead.

Corrupt PID files can crash `mlx-stack up` with an unhandled exception. `read_pid_file()` can raise `ProcessError` on non-numeric PID content (`src/mlx_stack/core/process.py:167-194`), but `_run_startup()` does not catch it when probing existing tier/litellm PIDs, and the CLI handler only catches `UpError`/`LockError` (`src/mlx_stack/cli/up.py:146-150`). This leaves a traceback path instead of graceful stale/corrupt PID cleanup.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The feature metadata requires `skillName: cli-feature`, and a skill file exists at `.factory/skills/cli-feature/SKILL.md`, but the worker transcript shows `Skill "cli-feature" not found` and the worker proceeded without it.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript skeleton for worker session `56acad8a-d59d-4541-8303-9964ade5f00f` includes `Tool: Skill {"skill":"cli-feature"}` followed by `Error: Skill "cli-feature" not found`; handoff `skillFeedback.deviations` repeats this.

summary: Review failed: two blocking issues were found in `up-command` (missing explicit missing-model handling and an unhandled corrupt-PID exception path). Shared-state note: `cli-feature` skill is referenced but not available at runtime.
